items.factory_architecture: **[$t(common:experiment_factory_arm)](/experiments/factory-arm).** A browser simulation of a robot arm unloading a pallet. One [WebSocket](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/WebSockets_API) per page carries [protobuf](https://protobuf.dev/) frames, chosen over [gRPC-Web](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-web) for bidirectional streaming. A [Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org/) bridge relays them to a digital twin in [NVIDIA Isaac Sim](https://developer.nvidia.com/isaac/sim) and answers “hold still” when it’s unreachable. Each session gets its own simulated rig, and the GPU machine stops itself when idle.
items.factory_arm: **[$t(common:experiment_factory_arm)](/experiments/factory-arm).** A browser-based robotic palletisation experiment. Planning runs in web workers, while a [Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org/) bridge relays [Protobuf](https://protobuf.dev/) frames over [WebSocket](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/WebSockets_API) to a digital twin running in [NVIDIA Isaac Sim](https://developer.nvidia.com/isaac/sim).
items.image_architecture: **[$t(common:experiment_image_agent)](/experiments/image-agent).** A public prompt-to-image agent with a fixed workflow. Every request passes four checks, cheapest first, and quotas are counted in [MongoDB](https://www.mongodb.com/) so a restart does not reset them. A reply cut short by a restart is marked failed when the conversation is next opened, so nobody is locked out.
items.image_frontend_ai: **[$t(common:experiment_image_agent)](/experiments/image-agent).** A public prompt-to-image agent, built to learn what it takes to put an AI feature in front of real people. A clarifier asks one question at a time, up to three, and code enforces the limit. The workflow is fixed in code as well, so the model never chooses its own tools. A vision model reviews each picture and can trigger one retry. Every request passes four checks, cheapest first: rate limits, rule checks, moderation and a small classifier. Quotas are counted in [MongoDB](https://www.mongodb.com/), and progress arrives over a [GraphQL](https://graphql.org/) subscription.
items.image_master: **[$t(common:experiment_image_agent)](/experiments/image-agent).** A public prompt-to-image agent that asks up to three clarifying questions, reviews generated images with a second model, and applies rate limits, rule checks, moderation and classification.
items.interpreter_react_native: **Interpreter (prototype).** A speech interpreter for two-way conversation. The [Expo](https://expo.dev/) app ([React Native](https://reactnative.dev/), [Tamagui](https://tamagui.dev/)) records push-to-talk audio and sends each utterance over a [WebSocket](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/WebSockets_API) to a [Fastify](https://fastify.dev/) server. The server detects the speaker's language, translates with [Claude](https://claude.com/) using the conversation so far, and streams captions back. The phone then speaks the result on-device. 21 languages, including Cantonese and Mandarin.
items.ki_architecture: **$t(projects.labels.ki).** A [React](https://react.dev/) host loads design-system, API-client and experiment remotes at runtime. The [GraphQL](https://graphql.org/) API ([Apollo Server](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/apollo-server/), [MongoDB](https://www.mongodb.com/)) sits behind a same-origin proxy that injects server-issued keys. Production runs on [Google Cloud Run](https://cloud.google.com/run).

items.ki_react_native: **$t(projects.labels.ki).** My personal platform, built as a federated architecture. A [React](https://react.dev/) host loads a design-system remote and typed [GraphQL](https://graphql.org/) client at runtime. Deployed on [Google Cloud Run](https://cloud.google.com/run).
items.tree_architecture: **[$t(common:experiment_tree_of_life)](/experiments/tree-of-life).** The [Open Tree of Life](https://tree.opentreeoflife.org/)’s 2.3 million species, cached in [MongoDB](https://www.mongodb.com/) as a parent-pointer tree with idempotent upserts, since lineages that share ancestors are written at once. Illustrations are generated in the background and arrive over a [GraphQL](https://graphql.org/) subscription. Text, image and vision calls each fail over across providers, with timeouts and cooldowns.
items.tree_frontend_ai: **[$t(common:experiment_tree_of_life)](/experiments/tree-of-life).** A walk through the [Open Tree of Life](https://tree.opentreeoflife.org/)’s 2.3 million species, cached in [MongoDB](https://www.mongodb.com/) as a parent-pointer tree. Illustrations are generated on demand by a fixed pipeline: resolve the lineage, pick a species, write the prompt, generate, score with a vision model, retry once. Text, image and vision calls each have their own provider failover chain, with timeouts and cooldowns.
items.tree_master: **[$t(common:experiment_tree_of_life)](/experiments/tree-of-life).** An interactive exploration of the [Open Tree of Life](https://tree.opentreeoflife.org/)’s 2.3 million species. Each organism’s illustration is generated on demand through a fixed AI pipeline with provider failover and vision-model review.
items.writing_frontend_ai: **Writing reviewer** (code only: $t(links.moonshot)). Reviews commit messages, pull-request descriptions and READMEs with [Claude](https://claude.com/). The model returns structured edits, each tied to a named rule. Code locates every quote and drops any edit that does not match exactly. It turns away prompt-injection attempts and has an eval set.
